newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Koor spinoff said unlikely until end-'98.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Koor spinoff said unlikely until end-'98.

text.p: Koor Industries Ltd.'s biggest shareholder, Bank Hapoalim, is not opposed to spinning off the Israeli conglomerate's biggest holdings but no action is likely until the end of 1998, Hapoalim sources said Sunday.
"It's an idea that has to be investigated...We haven't rejected it but we haven't accepted it," one Hapoalim source told Reuters.
But the sources added that it would be irresponsible to move forward with the proposal until state-owned Hapoalim was sold.
The Israeli government is in the midst of a tender to sell its controlling stake in Hapoalim, due to be completed in August, but could take longer.
Hapoalim sources said tax and legal considerations would require the spinoffs to be completed only at the end of the calender year.
"We said it can't be done this year," one source said regarding the Koor spinoff. "We put a time span of one year. If it can't be done this year, it will have to be done at the end of next year."

Confirming several days of speculation, Koor Chairman Stanley Gold said last Thursday he wanted to spin off Koor's biggest publicly traded companies to shareholders to enhance shareholder value. Gold is president of Shamrock Holdings Ltd., No. 2 shareholder.
Shamrock, a California-based investment company, controls 20 percent of Koor and Hapoalim holds a further 23 percent of Israel's biggest holding company.

Gold said his spinoff plan included Koor's holdings in Tadiran Ltd., Makhteshim Chemical Works, and Makhteshim's Agan Chemical Manufacturers subsidiary. The three are Koor's major publicly traded holdings.
Gold said his plan did not include transferring to shareholders closely held Nesher Cement, another major Koor holding.
Hapoalim sources said spinning off the listed subsidiaries would be easier from a tax point of view since their value was set by the market.
They said, in any case, that a major divestiture like the one Gold was proposing would require a ruling from the Israeli authorities on tax treatment before they could go ahead.

Bank Leumi undertook a similar transaction last year, spinning off Leumi Insurance Holdings Ltd. from Africa Israel Investments Ltd. The spinoff enabled Italy's Assicurazioni Generali SpA to acquire control of Leumi Insurance.

A Hapoalim spokeswoman said Sunday the bank had no comment on the reports. A Koor spokesman would not comment specifically on reports but said: "The management of Koor Industries acts on guidelines set by Koor directors."

The Hapoalim sources said their view of the spin-off plan would not be coloured by the $140 million loan Shamrock took to finance the acquisition of its Koor stake in March 1995. Analysts have said the bank might prefer to keep the loan on its books than accept shares.

"I think we have two entirely separate issues that will be dealt with by different people at different times," one source said, adding it was unclear whether Shamrock would use the divestiture to bail out of Koor.
The sources said Hapoalim and Shamrock were not disappointed with Koor's profitability. "Shamrock is more disappointed by the performance of the shares than of the company," a source said.
The holding company's American Depository Receipts, traded on the New York Stock Exchange, closed at $18 on Friday.
